tip: Piacere literally means "to be pleasing": "Mi piace il caffè" = Coffee is pleasing to me. Subject comes after.

english: Have you ever been to Italy?
tip: In a question mai means ever: sei mai stato, have you ever been. With non it flips to never.

target: Come si arriva in centro a piedi?
english: How do you get downtown on foot?
tip: Impersonal si plus a verb means a general you or one: come si arriva = how do you get there.
"Uno" is the indefinite article for masculine nouns before s+consonant, z, gn, ps.
Weather uses fare, not essere: fa caldo means it is hot, and fa freddo means it is cold.
Nouns ending in -e give no gender clue; esame is masculine: un esame, gli esami.
Masculine plural uses gli before a vowel or s plus consonant: gli specchi, gli amici.
cadere forms the past with essere, so the participle agrees: un albero è caduto, una foglia è caduta.
For rates, Italian uses a plus the article: al giorno means per day, due volte al giorno is twice a day.
frutta is a singular collective meaning fruit in general; a single piece is un frutto.
mano is feminine even though it ends in -o, and its plural is le mani.
problema is masculine despite the -a ending, like most words in -ma; the plural is i problemi.
radio never changes in the plural: la radio and le radio stay identical.
braccio is masculine in the singular but its plural braccia is feminine: le braccia stanche.
To keep the hard g sound, words ending in -go add an h in the plural: largo becomes larghi.
Masculine nouns starting with s plus consonant take lo, not il: lo stivale, lo studente.
Words stressed on a final vowel never change in the plural: la pubblicità, le pubblicità.
To make a verb negative, put non right before it: non scrive means it does not write.
The suffix -ina makes a small version: from busta, an envelope, you get bustina, a little packet.
salata literally means salty, but for a bill or fine it means steep: la multa è salata.
When molto modifies a verb it means a lot and stays invariable: studia molto.
chiedere already means to ask for, so no preposition follows: chiede informazioni.
Add -issimo, or -issime in the feminine plural, to mean very: verdissime means very green.
funzionare is to work for machines and devices; use lavorare for people: i semafori non funzionano.

english: The man walks in the park.
tip: in plus il contracts to nel: nel parco means in the park.
For aches, use mi fa male plus the body part; the part is the subject, so fa stays singular: mi fa male la testa.
When the aching body part is plural, use fanno instead of fa: mi fanno male i piedi.
a plus gli contracts to agli: agli italiani means to the Italians.
ricetta means recipe, but ricetta medica is a doctor's prescription.
Like piacere, verbs like interessare, mancare, servire use indirect object pronouns: "Mi manca" = I miss (it).
